title: Quantifying Annotation Agreement in Object Detection with Optimal Transport

problem.summary: Modern machine learning systems rely on annotated data for training and validation, typically treating a fixed test set as a gold standard.

evidence.quote: Modern machine learning systems rely on annotated data for training and validation, typically treating a fixed test set as a gold standard.
Yet a single noise-free ground truth may not exist: multiple plausible annotations can arise from task ambiguity, limited visual evidence, or differences in expert judgment.

components: Yet a single noise-free ground truth may not exist: multiple plausible annotations can arise from task ambiguity, limited visual evidence, or differences in expert judgment.
This is especially relevant in object detection, where annotators may disagree on object presence, spatial extent, or class labels [4, 14, 21].
Such disagreement contains information about the reliability of the reference data.
